title: Russian alphabet and pronunciation
keywords: russian alphabet cyrillic letters vowels consonants pronunciation hard sign soft sign чтение
text: Russian uses 33 Cyrillic letters. The alphabet includes vowels, consonants, the semivowel Й, and the hard and soft signs Ъ and Ь. The signs do not represent standalone spoken sounds; they influence how adjacent sounds are read. First learn letters in everyday words, then practise stress and pronunciation.

title: Introduction to learning Russian
keywords: russian learn study beginner course textbook reading writing immersion
text: A beginner course benefits from learning Cyrillic early, reading and writing short lines, and practising with native speakers. Work through letters, everyday dialogues, basic grammar and reviews. Reading authentic Russian material gradually improves fluency; a textbook alone cannot replace conversation practice.

title: Russian greetings and introductions
keywords: russian greetings hello privet здравствуйте привет hello formal informal introduction name how are you
text: Привет (privet) is an informal greeting; Здравствуйте (zdravstvuyte) is formal or polite. Меня зовут ... is the standard way to say My name is ...; Как тебя зовут? asks informally for someone's name. Как дела? asks How are things?; Хорошо answers Fine. Use ты with friends and вы in formal situations.

title: Six Russian grammatical cases
keywords: russian grammar cases nouns endings nominative genitive dative accusative instrumental prepositional падеж
text: Russian traditionally teaches six principal cases: nominative for subjects, genitive for possession and some negation, dative for recipients, accusative for direct objects, instrumental for means and accompaniment, and prepositional for many location or discussion phrases. Case endings change nouns and agreeing modifiers; context and prepositions determine which ending to use.

title: Russian verb aspect
keywords: russian grammar verbs aspect perfective imperfective делать сделать писать написать action completed
text: Russian verbs distinguish imperfective and perfective aspect. Imperfective often describes repeated activity, ongoing process or an action without focus on completion. Perfective usually stresses a completed result or bounded event. For example, делать and сделать both relate to doing, while писать and написать relate to writing; the choice of aspect depends on what the speaker wishes to emphasize.

title: Russian grammar study map
keywords: russian grammar cases gender plural pronouns adjectives verbs tense noun declension
text: A practical grammar sequence covers noun gender and plurals, the six cases, agreement of adjectives and pronouns, then verbs and tense. Russian lacks English-style a and the articles. Learning common case endings alongside example sentences is more useful than memorizing isolated tables.

title: Wiktionary formal and informal greetings
keywords: dictionary russian здравствуй здравствуйте привет greeting hello formal informal pronunciation
text: The Russian greeting здравствуй is informal singular hello; здравствуйте is used for formal address or multiple people. Привет is a casual alternative. Wiktionary provides pronunciation, inflection and etymological context for individual terms; verify stress and regional usage in its source entries.
